MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  CITY OF NORWALK
  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  August 4, 2025

Chair LeGaspi called the meeting to order at 6:04 p.m. in the Council Chambers, Norwalk
City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Responding to the roll call were
Chair LeGaspi, Vice Chair Rosoff, Commissioner Apodaca, Commissioner Hoskins,
Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez and Commissioner Greenidge. Also, present was Rita Ruiz,
Interim Director and Veronica Lomas, Management Analyst.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Commissioner Hoskins motioned for the approval of the minutes of the Public Safety
Commission Meeting minutes that was held on July 7, 2025. Vice Chair Rosoff seconded
the motion.

MOTION CARRIED BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

AYES:  Chair LeGaspi, Vice Chair Rosoff, Commissioner Apodaca,
  Commissioner Hoskins, Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez, Commissioner
  Greenidge and Commissioner Fernandez-Silva
NOES:  None
ABSENT: None
ABSTAIN: None

REPORTS

4th of July Illegal Firework Enforcement Results

Mrs. Lomas provided the Commission with a report on the results of the 4th of July
enforcement operation. She noted that some officers utilized dash cameras to assist in
issuing citations for illegal fireworks. Calls regarding fireworks activity leading up to the
holiday were relatively low, which can be attributed to community education and outreach
efforts, the illegal fireworks hotline, and proactive patrols in known hot spots. The report
also highlighted that 60 administrative citations were issued, and Public Safety Officers
responded to 83 calls for service.

Blue Curb Application– 15508 Studebaker Rd.

Mrs. Lomas provided a report regarding a Blue Curb request at 15508 Studebaker Road.
The applicant, Ms. Estefania Martin Del Campo, was not in attendance at the meeting.
Following a thorough evaluation and on-site inspection, Ms. Martin Del Campo’s
application was denied. The request did not meet the criteria outlined in Norwalk
Municipal Code Section 10.10.060. Specifically:
 E. The applicant’s garage may not be used for storage, and the property must be free
from any code violations.

F. On-site parking spaces must be used for parking operable vehicles and may not be
used for storage of inoperable or abandoned vehicles, as described in Chapter 8.12. (Ord.
22-1730 § 1; Ord. 21-1722 § 2; Ord. 16-1677 § 1)

Blue Curb Application– 12313 Everest St.

Mrs. Lomas provided a report regarding a Blue Curb request at 12313 Everest. The
applicant, Mr. Patrick Brady, was not in attendance at the meeting. Following a thorough
evaluation and on-site inspection, Mr. Brady’s application was denied. The request did
not meet the criteria outlined in Norwalk Municipal Code Section 10.10.060. Specifically:

E. The applicant’s garage may not be used for storage, and the property must be free
from any code violations.

F. On-site parking spaces must be used for parking operable vehicles, as described in
Chapter 8.12. (Ord. 22-1730 § 1; Ord. 21-1722 § 2; Ord. 16-1677 § 1)

Blue Curb Application– 12024 164th Street

Mrs. Lomas provided a report regarding a Blue Curb request at 12024 164th Street. The
applicant, Ms. Thuong Phia, was not in attendance at the meeting. Following a thorough
evaluation and on-site inspection, Ms. Phia’s application was denied. The request did not
meet the criteria outlined in Norwalk Municipal Code Section 10.10.060. Specifically:

B. No application will be accepted and processed unless all required information is
provided.

E. The applicant’s garage may not be used for storage, and the property must be free
from any code violations.

F. On-site parking spaces must be used for parking operable vehicles, as described in
Chapter 8.12. (Ord. 22-1730 § 1; Ord. 21-1722 § 2; Ord. 16-1677 § 1)

That concluded the Blue Curb reports.

The Commission then viewed a video highlighting recent special events and monthly
activities.

Lastly, the Commission discussed the development of a mission and vision statement for
the Public Safety Commission, along with establishing minimum requirements and duties
for commissioners. Input is being sought from each commissioner regarding what should
be included. This discussion will continue through commission roundtable and email
correspondence with Chair Legaspi, Vice Chair Rosoff, and Commissioner Greenidge.
 STAFF COMMENTS

Mrs. Lomas went over the August 2025 calendar and provided an updated Advisory Body
Packet.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS
Commissioner Fernandez-Silva and Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez commented on the
Blue Curb application process, the appeal procedure, and whether applicants are
provided an opportunity to correct violations. Mrs. Lomas explained the process and
appeal procedure, noting that each applicant receives a letter advising them of the
decision. The Commission agreed with the staff’s recommendation and decision.
Commissioner Rosoff inquired about street sweeping enforcement, noting that Public
Safety Officers do not consistently follow the street sweeping truck. He also raised the
possibility of installing cameras on street sweeping vehicles to capture violations and
issue citations.

Commissioner Greenidge mentioned observing patrols by LASD and Public Safety
Officers in response to her neighbor Angela’s concern, raised at last month’s meeting,
regarding vehicles failing to stop at stop signs on Mapledale and Flallon.

ADJOURNMENT:

Being no further business to come before the Public Safety Commission, the meeting was
adjourned at 7:13 PM.

_______________________________
CHAIR
Richard LeGaspi
